title: Orlando Pirates and Durban City draw in match full of chances
seoTitle: Orlando Pirates, Durban City draw in chance-filled match
subtitle: Match marked by high pressure, yellow cards, and wasted opportunities
excerpt: In the 7th round of the Betway Premiership, Orlando Pirates and Durban City drew 0-0 after a first half full of attacks, fouls, and yellow cards, keeping the.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
In the 7th round of the Betway Premiership, Orlando Pirates and Durban City faced each other at Orlando Stadium and ended the first half goalless, despite numerous chances created by both teams.

Pressure and opportunities in the first half

The Pirates started the match imposing an intense pace, keeping possession in the attacking third and trying to open the scoring with long-range shots. Jean Lwamba received a pass from Jurgens and fired from outside the box, but the ball was deflected for a corner. Gastón Sirino also tried, sending a powerful shot into the right corner, saved by Chaine.

Fouls and yellow cards

The match was marked by harsh challenges. Jurgens received a yellow card for a foul on Mokobodi, and Brooklyn Poggenpoel was booked for a heavy tackle on Masilela. Later, Lwamba and Mthiyane were also shown yellow cards for fouls in midfield.

Corners and wasted chances

The Pirates won a corner that caused a scramble inside the box, but Nkosinathi Sibisi shot wide. In another opportunity, Ncanana received a cross and his shot was blocked by the Durban City defense. Despite the attempts, none of the shots found the back of the net.

Positioning and formations

Both teams lined up in a 4-2-3-1 formation. Orlando Pirates started with Chaine; Sebelebele, Seema, Sibisi, and Ndaba in defense; Mthiyane and Mokobodi in midfield; Kgositsile, Masilela, and Moremi in attack; and Mbuthuma as the main striker. Durban City fielded Asare, Gcaba, Ncanana, Msomi, and Mokone in defense; Jurgens and Poggenpoel in midfield; Sirino, Sanger, and Lwamba up front.

Standings and tournament outlook

With the draw, Orlando Pirates remain in second place in the Betway Premiership with 13 points, seven behind leaders Mamelodi Sundowns, who have played three more games. Durban City, now with six points, occupy ninth place, tied with Stellenbosch and TS Galaxy.

The clash showcased the Pirates' attacking capability and Durban City's defensive resilience, leaving the match wide open for the second half, where the first goal could change the course of the table.

With information from VAVEL.com.
